text:
The repetition of "structures" does not add any information to the already more specific term "social structures".
If this repetition was intended it would have to be comma-separated.
I guess this is just a typo.

The title and subtitle are not in title case
To improve readability of the title and, and to be consistent with the usual style for scientific publications, I recommend the use of title case in English
Since this is an embedded sentence, you should use commas before and after it, to improve readability.
Since the term "emotional coexistence" is not standardized, you may want to discuss it within your Exposé to clarify what you mean by it.
This part of the title is clear, easy to understand and precisely reflects your work

The hook is hard to understand.
Without the embedded sentence the hook basically says that the relationships between humans and AI partners open a new dimension of human relationships.
It is hard to understand which entities are exactly referred by "are both exciting and terrifying". Maybe the plural here is a typo.

You could optimize readability and clarity by using singular terms and avoid repeating relationships: "The relationship between humans and holographic AI partners [...] opens up a new dimension to human interaction, both exiting and terifying. "

This anecdote clarifies your topic and makes it very relatable and convincing without a lot of explanation needed. Maybe you want to use this as the first sentence of your Exposé and replace "such technologies" with the explaining embedded sentence.
To further support this, you couldcite a source explaining the contents of the movie with focus on the human - AI relationship.

"however" implies that some kind of contradiction or dissent is present. Since the real world technology is actually evolving in the same direction as the movie, no contradiction is present.  Thus the word "however" is inapplicable here.

You may avoid using word combinations that can be replaced by a single precise word. This aligns with the formal tone in academic texts, reduces verbosity and conciseness.
To find appropriate words to replace less formal terms like "and so" I recommend to use a thesaurus, e.g. thesaurus.com
Try to avoid repeating phrases, as this can make the text less concise, and reduce the reader's engagement.
the vocab supports your depiction of the research gap and is therefore well chosen

This phrase lacks formal tone as it is a bit vague about what "much" is.
Maybe use "Has not been extensively studied" or "has received limited attention in research"
Acceptability to which measures? Maybe use "societal acceptability" to clarify that it is not about e.g. ecological footprint

Your citations belong in the text, at the points where you state claims that need support of these citations.
This part of the template was only to demonstrate how to cite with Latex. To have your cited literature in the bibliography listed automatically, use the \cite{my_paper} command anywhere in your text.
If you don't want to go with the [n] citation format within your text and stay with the (name et. al.) format, you have to create your bibliography manually as new chapter.
Please remove the Example keyword from the template as this is your preliminary schedule and not some generic example anymore.
This sentence part clearly highlights what your research is about

Taking away the embedded sentence you say "As mentioned in Rauschnabel, these studies have led me to question ..." As if you were mentioned in the study of Rauschnabel.
I guess you meant "Rauschnabel investigated [...] with holograms. This study led me to question [...]"

To easiliy improve clarity, you can simply change some dots and commas here:
"Furthermore, recent research [...] of such technologies, [Dot -> Comma] as mentioned in Rauschnabel [...] with holograms. [Comma -> Dot] These studies have [...]"

Physical products are always objects, mentioning objects as an example therefore is redundant. You could remove the "such as objects" phrase or specify more precisely by using "tangible products" instead of "physical products"
When using "emotional beings such as humans" you have to use plural -> "which are"

Since humans are just mentioned here as an example for emotional beings, this opens up the research gap of adapting the topic to other emotional beings, such as elephants, whales, primates and other organisms for which evidence exists that they have capacities to show emotion.
You could cite a source that describes the evolvement of AI technologies regarding emotional relationships.
You should cite Rauschnabel right here as this is the sentence in which you state the claim.

When mentioning research gaps in the existing literature it is always better to cite sources that state these gaps (e.g. as future work) instead of just claiming them. If in your case, you don't find sources that state research primarily focused on products and there is a gap for the focus on humans, you could instead cite surveys that give an overview of product-centric studies.
Citing will support your claim as makes it reproducible for the reader without having to be an expert on the topic or having to undertake a literature review themself.

In short, you wrote that the research gap calls for investigation, thus it has enormous relevance. This is contradicting as it would mean that every existing research gap has enormous relevance.
You should support the claim of enormous relevance e.g. by citing statistics about the increased use of AI partners.
This claim needs to be supported by source that comes to this prediction. Otherwise it is a personal prediction which does not align with neutral and objective tone in scientific writing.
You could cite a statistic that supports this claim

In short you write, due to the rapid development you will examine the potential dangers. This suggests that only due to the rapid development AI poses potential dangers that need to be addressed. This would mean that if there was no rapid development there would not be any potential dangers. As this is not true the sentence may be contradicting.

Avoid using the first person to match scientific tone. Instead of writing "I" or "me" describe the process (e.g. "this leads to the question") or use the plural form if not avoidable (e.g. "has led us to the question")
Avoid using the first person to match scientific tone
Avoid using the first person to match scientific tone
Avoid using the first person to match scientific tone
Avoid using the first person to match scientific tone
Avoid using the first person to match scientific tone. You used the same word to begin two successive sentences. Avoid such repititions as they may reduce reader engagement.
Introducing meaningful abbreviations can improve readability. Explaining them early in the text helps the reader as they don't have to look them up theirself.
To support this claim you could cite literature describing such systems or link to existing proucts.

You should cite literature that comes to this conclusion. Alternatively you could just mention that the integration of AI into holographic displays has the potential to enable more sophisticated emotional interaction without claiming it to be actually achieved.
You have to add citations to such claims within the text in order to enable the reader to understand with source belongs to which claim.
A citation supporting this claim is missing here
A citation supporting this claim is missing here

Such systems could help
revolutionize virtual interactions in various areas, including gaming, education and therapy.
A citation supporting the claim is missing.

it is not clear what "This" refers to in this sentence. Is it the adaption to the user's emotional state or is it the virtual character itself?
You can clarify it by using "This adaption" instead.
A citation supporting this claim is missing.
MAXQDA is a well known, well researched software for qualitative data analysis
This is the main research question
This is a sub research question
This is a sub research question

Did you mean target groups? (Plural)
If not, then it is not clear how the actual target group is chosen out of the groups you mentioned.

Which hypothesis is tested?
According to your RQ you want to test if holographic AI partners with reshape our social values, normas, interpersonal relationships, if these technologies are capable of building emotional bonds and what dangers they may pose to social structures and human interactions.
Contradicting to it you mention hypotheses on user acceptance, which itself is not part of your research question and you forgot to state actual hypotheses to test for.

How do you assess technical knowledge and social attitudes and how do you use them in evaluation? You should clarify whether you use a likert-scale questionnaire, a quiz, a social experiment, shock therapy, ...
In order to be able to assess technical knowledge and especially social attitudes, you should define or cite theoretical frameworks to which they can be evaluated.
When using SPSS only for evaluating the survey, you should clarify that it is assessing quanitative data only, e.g. by specifying the online survey as questionnaire with likert scale questions only.
SPSS is a well known, well researched software for finding statistically significant corellations.

Please describe how the methodology is answering the research questions by referring to them and precisely describing your methods. Mentioning that the methodology will somehow magically be tailored to be suitable is not sufficient, even at the early stage of an Exposé.

By mentioning the fields of which experts are included as participants and by mentioning that potential users are also included as participants, you ensured that both perspecives are taken into account
This repetition may reduce conciseness and reader engagement.

You may want to mention the approaches explicitly (e.g. "qualitative interviews and quantitative online surveys"), as at this point "both approaches" could be mistakenly interpreted as the approach to ask expert and the approach to ask potential users. However, the next sentence states that you mean qualitative and quantitative approaches.
Your reasoning about why which target groups were included is solid. The chosen target groups support your research aim.

The sentence itself does not describe why or how the groups are defined with due care, so information is missing, but completed by the explanation in the next sentence. So linking these two sentences by combining them with comma or ":" may improve readability.
Good vocab that signalizes the integrity of your work
You may want to clarify on how you contact participants. Especially using social networks may introduce ethical risks that you should to consider (e.g. by using micro-targeting).

You should have used an established or created a new theoretical framework for your Exposé already. You can further refine it when conducting your work, but the theories you use and how they combine with your experiments should be at least described rudimentarily in the Exposé.
You already formulated research questions in your Motivation chapter, so you don't have to mention formulating them in the methodology as they should already be clear.
You mentioned issues that may arise during your work and potential solutions on how to handle them.

When ending your text with a summary, you should rather summarize your research topic and methodology and not write that your text fulfills the given rating criteria. Just fulfill it within your text.
Honestly, this paragraph reads like an AI-written justification to the rating criteria of the methodology section.
You may remove it completely.
You have defined research questions in your Exposé. This should not be a task to do anymore.

You have designed the survey questions, but as you mentioned that the survey will be held online, you should also regard the implementation of the online survey as a task.
Maybe you want to add this to scenario planning or do it in parallel to recruiting.
"organizing" is vague here as your data is organized in some way at this point. You may want to mention pre-filtering outliers, preparation of data to required formats, ...
To improve clarity you could add the word "chapter"

Buffer time is not be reserved for printing and submission, but for all unplanned tasks that may occur before that.
Simply replace "for" with a comma to correctly signalize this.

I guess the existing material you are regarding is the literature that should have been cited in your SOTA. But as this should be current scientific literature and studies, to mention them again is redundant.

As you clearly stated that your topic is not researched much, I don't think that existing literature will be suitable as a benchmark. From what I understand the whole point of your research is to fill a gap that is in your words "largely unconsidered". When assuming that to be true, there won't be sufficient research so benchmark against.
Besides that, the question is on how to benchmark against the research, as you did not mention any theories or scales that could be tested against.
The method to use qualitative interviews is well described with type of interview, the potential participants and the aims of the interviews.

What does the online survey ask besides age, technical knowledge and social attitutes? Please go a bit more into detail about which aspects of acceptance are assessed to which aspects of holographic AI. Maybe you can find a standard questionnaire on the acceptance of AI systems and on holographic user interfaces or create a new one.
Having a theroetical framework which you could refer to when assessing certain aspects of a theory would largely help to understand what you're actually researching.

As this is a blog post of the CEO of a display company, it may be not a trustworthy source. The author has not published any scientific literature. The blog post should be understood as advertising measure, despite the fact that it explains the technology. It should therefore not be used as a source for a scientific work.

This question leads to a yes/no answer. You should rather use wording that allows for complex answers e.g. "To which extent these technologies are capable of building emotional bonds"
remove this to better match scientific tone

As you stated that there is a lack on research for your topic in order to clarify the research gap, being able to close it by doing a comprehensive literature review alone would contradict to the existence of the research gap in the first place. Stick to your methodology in the approach section when writing about how to answer the research question.
To clarify that "this topic" is referring to your anker / your work, you could use "This work" instead.

did you mean "psychotherapy"?
Therapy without a context can mean lots of things. For example I don't see how these systems could help with acne therapy ;)
Avoid repetitions to improve conciceseness and readability
to match the scientific tone, remove this magnification.

Your Sota reads more like you're rattling off a list of technologies than combining them to paint an overall picture. You mention AI driven technologies which reads as if they would be about AI avatars/partners but the neural networks in them are just used for optical reasons. The only exception to this is the claim about AR systems that are developed with the aim to create appealing and responsive avatars.
You should clearly differentiate between AI used for optics and AI used for avatars as your research questions are not about the technical implementation of holographic optics.
You used future tense here. In academic work you should always try to use present tense

Besides some minor flaws in some task descriptions and a rather short time period planned for implementing the online survey, your schedule looks really good, as it is planned on a realistic timescale and contains  all relevant tasks.
